result.summary: The image depicts a wide urban arterial with multiple travel lanes and integrated light rail tracks, creating a high-speed environment. While sidewalks are present and in good condition, the significant crossing distance and lack of mid-block protection or traffic calming measures prioritize vehicle throughput over pedestrian safety.

hazards.name: Excessive Crossing Distance
hazards.description: Pedestrians must cross multiple travel lanes and light rail tracks at the intersection, increasing exposure time to traffic.

hazards.name: Driveway Conflict Point
hazards.description: A wide driveway entrance for a commercial property creates a conflict point where turning vehicles cross the pedestrian walkway.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side of the image near the Dunkin' sign

hazards.name: High-Speed Roadway Design
hazards.description: Wide, straight travel lanes and a lack of vertical traffic calming elements encourage higher vehicle speeds.
hazards.location_in_image: Main roadway lanes in the foreground and center

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install curb extensions (bulb-outs) at the intersection to reduce crossing distance and improve visibility between drivers and pedestrians.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Refuge Island
interventions.description: Incorporate a raised refuge island between the light rail tracks and the travel lanes to allow pedestrians to cross in stages.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Upgrade standard transverse crosswalk markings to high-visibility continental or ladder patterns.

interventions.title: Protected Bike Lanes
interventions.description: Repurpose a portion of the wide roadway for protected bicycle lanes, which would also serve to narrow the travel lanes and slow traffic.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment is highly auto-oriented, dominated by a large surface parking lot with multiple wide vehicle access points that cross the sidewalk. There is a complete lack of physical separation or buffering between pedestrians and the high-speed roadway or the parking area.

hazards.name: Excessive Curb Cuts
hazards.description: Multiple wide driveways create frequent conflict points where vehicles cross the pedestrian path, often at higher speeds due to the lack of narrowing.
hazards.location_in_image: Across the entire frontage of the commercial property

hazards.name: Lack of Pedestrian Buffer
hazards.description: No physical separation or green space exists between the sidewalk and the roadway or the parking lot, exposing pedestrians to traffic splash and noise.
hazards.location_in_image: Along the edge of the roadway and parking lot

interventions.title: Driveway Consolidation
interventions.description: Reduce the number and width of curb cuts to minimize conflict points and provide a more continuous, protected walkway.

interventions.title: Landscape Buffer
interventions.description: Install a planting strip or street trees between the sidewalk and the roadway to provide physical separation and improve the pedestrian experience.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Narrow the roadway at potential crossing points to reduce pedestrian exposure and slow turning vehicles.

result.summary: The environment is dominated by a wide, multi-lane arterial road with long crossing distances and minimal pedestrian protection. While sidewalks are present, they lack significant buffers from high-speed traffic and are frequently interrupted by commercial driveways.

hazards.description: The wide multi-lane roadway requires pedestrians to cross a significant distance without any refuge islands or mid-block crossings.

hazards.name: Frequent Driveway Conflicts
hazards.description: Multiple curb cuts for parking lots and businesses create numerous conflict points between pedestrians and turning vehicles.

hazards.name: Lack of Pedestrian Buffer
hazards.description: The sidewalk is directly adjacent to the travel lanes or parking lane with no physical barrier or planting strip to protect pedestrians.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Refuge Island
interventions.description: Install a raised median or refuge island to allow pedestrians to cross one direction of traffic at a time.

interventions.description: Construct bulb-outs at intersections or mid-block to reduce crossing distance and improve visibility between drivers and pedestrians.

interventions.title: Street Trees and Landscaping

result.summary: The pedestrian environment is characterized by a wide, multi-lane arterial road with minimal physical separation between the walkway and high-speed traffic. The streetscape is dominated by large surface parking lots and blank frontages, which lack active uses and provide no buffer for pedestrians.

hazards.name: Excessive Crossing Distance
hazards.description: The wide multi-lane roadway requires pedestrians to cross a significant distance without a refuge island or mid-block crossing.

hazards.name: Lack of Pedestrian Buffer
hazards.description: The sidewalk is directly adjacent to the travel lanes with no trees, parked cars, or furniture zone to protect pedestrians from traffic.

hazards.name: Frequent Driveway Conflicts
hazards.description: Large surface parking lots create multiple points where vehicles cross the sidewalk, increasing the risk of collisions.
hazards.location_in_image: Left and right sides of the roadway

interventions.title: Street Trees and Planting Strips
interventions.description: Install a line of street trees or a landscaped buffer between the sidewalk and the curb to provide physical and psychological separation from traffic.

interventions.title: Mid-Block Pedestrian Crossing
interventions.description: Install a high-visibility marked crosswalk with a pedestrian refuge island and potentially a HAWK signal to facilitate safe crossing.

interventions.title: Road Diet
interventions.description: Reduce the number of through lanes or narrow existing lanes to reclaim space for a protected bike lane or wider sidewalk buffer, which naturally slows vehicle speeds.
